insight.title: Why Things Cost More Over Time
insight.subtitle: Understanding the invisible forces that drive our global economy.

sections.text: Imagine you are at a market with ten apples and twenty hungry people. Because everyone wants an apple, the seller raises the price. This simple dance between how much exists and how many people want it governs almost everything you buy. When supply is low and demand is high, prices naturally climb upward.

Now, imagine the government prints more money for everyone. Suddenly, you have more cash, but the number of apples stays the same. Since everyone can pay more, the seller raises prices again. This is why things cost more over time. Your money feels less powerful because there is simply more of it circulating.

Technology changes this game by making production easier. If a farmer invents a machine to grow a hundred apples instead of ten, the price drops. Businesses constantly compete to find cheaper ways to make goods. This balance of money, supply, and innovation is what keeps our global economy moving every single day.
